## Reach — what the registry can even see

Everything above is bounded by this. A pair hangs off a context, and a source file in no
context can never be judged however good the corpus is. Run
`node scripts/check-context-coverage.mjs` for the per-project table; the headline is that
coverage is a property of each project's own `context-map.json`, which this registry cannot
regenerate — the fix is `/project-populate` over there.

Two failure directions, and only one of them has ever been reported: the map counts
`contextsWithMissingPaths` (contexts pointing at files that are gone) and has no field at
all for files that no context points at, which is the larger number in every project
measured. Note also that a published map carries a **twelve-path sample** per context
(`build-registry-map.mjs` slices to 12 while matching against up to 60), so "this file is
in no context" read off the map alone is not a safe conclusion — read `context-map.json`.

**judged %** is the share of pairs any pass has actually read the code for. `unknown` is not
conformance; it is the absence of a verdict. **misses** are commits whose governing subject was
not read, recorded by `consult-check`; a project with 0 consults AND 0 misses is not compliant,
it is uninstrumented.

## Undeclared checkouts

These carry `.ai/manifest.yaml`, have already written a consult or lead ledger, and are
absent from `projects.json` — so every collector resolves them to nothing without erroring,
and whatever they learned cannot arrive.

- `kiro/bp`
